catalog_quote: La langue songola est classée en D-23 par Guthrie (1967) et appelée "binja-N" par Meeussen (1951 m.s.). Le bembe est semblable au songola, et tous deux ont sept voyelles /ị i e a o u ụ/. [...] Toutes les langues citées sont tonales; elles ont un ton haut "´" et un ton bas "`". (p. 6) — 4) Les Enya de Kindu n'ont pas d'ascendance commune avec les Enya de Kisangani et ils n'ont pas de liens étroits avec ceux de Kasongo. Les premiers ont perdu leur langue d'origine et actuellement ils emploient soit le songola (binja-N), soit l'ombo, d'après leur position géographique. [...] 5) Les tons des mots enya ont été relevés comme suit: Les informateurs ont été priés d'ajouter "mon" (-ané) à chacun des noms de poisson, ce qui a rendu les tons clairs et stables. L'emploi d'un tambour-signal à fente traditionnel (lùkúmbí) a facilité leur notation. (p. 41) — Ankei 1989 p. 5: All these are tone languages having principally a high tone and a low tone. [...] Table 2A. Phonemes of Songola-Enya and Bwari. [...] tones: High: /´/. Low: without tone marks, except for consonants having one mora such as /ḿ/ and /ń/.

new_statements.translation: The Songola language is classed as D-23 by Guthrie (1967) and called "binja-N" by Meeussen (1951 ms). Bembe is similar to Songola, and both have seven vowels /ị i e a o u ụ/. [...] All the languages cited are tonal; they have a high tone "´" and a low tone "`". — The Enya of Kindu have no common ancestry with the Enya of Kisangani and no close ties with those of Kasongo. The former have lost their original language and at present use either Songola (binja-N) or Ombo, according to their geographical position.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened and Persée renderPage images of Ankei 1986a, Africana Linguistica 10) and read them visually, plus the held scanned. Sec. 1.3 'Langues', p. 6, reads exactly: 'La langue songola est classée en D-23 par Guthrie (1967) et appelée "binja-N" par Meeussen (1951 m.s.). Le bembe est semblable au songola, et tous deux ont sept voyelles /ị i e a o u ụ/. Le vira est classé en J-55 par Bastin (1975) (3). [..] Toutes les langues citées sont tonales; elles ont un ton haut "´" et un ton bas "`".' Note 4, p. 41, reads exactly as quoted ('Les Enya de Kindu n'ont pas d'ascendance commune avec les Enya de Kisangani.. soit le songola (binja-N), soit l'ombo, d'après leur position géographique.'); note 5…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language of the Enya fishers near Kindu (= Glottolog Enya-Kindu; Ankei's Enya-subgroup dialect of Songola/binja-N) is a two-tone language (H vs L), with low tone on noun-class prefixes (Ankei 1982: 3, Table 1; 1986b: 245); no source says anything about word stress or accent, so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements refer to lexical items (fish and mammal names) in citation form, elicited near Kindu 1978-1983 with a possessive frame (-ané 'my') and checked against slit-drum renditions (1986a n. 5, p. 41). Ankei 1982 Table 1 (p. 3) gives the phoneme inventory of the Enya-subgroup dialect specifically; 1986b p. 245 describes the Kuko dialect. Tone only; no stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's Enya-Kindu (enya1249, no ISO code) is defined via Bastin et al. 1999 (Enya at Kibombo and Manda) and Ankei's 'Enya of Tongomacho'/'Enya Songola' (hh.bib lgcodes map Ankei's Enya Songola and Kuko to Enya-Kindu). Ankei himself (1986a n. 4, p. 41; 1982 p. 2) says the Enya of Kindu lost their original language and now speak a dialect of Songola (binja-N; Guthrie D.23/24) or Ombo; his phoneme table (1982 p. 3) is labelled 'Enya-subgroup dialect of Songola' and 1986b describes the Kuko dialect. So the opened statements describe the Songola-dialect speech of the Kindu Enya, which Glottolog treats as Enya-Kindu, distinct from Songola/Songoora proper (song1300) and from Enya-Kisangani (enya1247, ISO gey; Spa 1973). Bukungu Batangana 1981 'kigenya' (ISP Kindu) is filed under gey but unverified.

sources.note: Sec. 1.3.1 部族語, p. 3, Table 1 'ソンゴーラ語エニャ支族方言の音素 (A) と名詞のクラス (B)' (phonemes and noun classes of the Enya-subgroup dialect of Songola, from the author's own fieldwork): vowels /i̧ i e a o u u̧/, semivowels y w, consonants m n ny ŋ / b l nj ng / p t s ch k; 'トーン 高 /´/ 低 /`/' (tone: high, low); 'prefix のトーンは低 /`/ である' (prefixes carry low tone). p. 4: '以上4つの言語は,いずれも高低のトーンをもつ言語である' (all four languages have high/low tone). Nothing on stress or accent (アクセント absent from the whole text). This is the original of which Ankei 1986a is the abridged French version (1986a n. 1).
